name: Store transaction deterioration
phase8_metric: Transactions per store YoY, store vs its matched peer stores
phase8_baseline: The store's own gap to its peers over the previous 13 weeks
phase8_threshold: A step change in the gap that persists (change-point test as in Phase 6); size and persistence rules to be calibrated
implemented_metric: Peer gap: log(store transactions / same week last year) minus log(all other stores' transactions / same week last year)
grain_reason: Stores are where a local shock (like S03-S05) shows first. Store x category would add noise without a new question; region and format roll-ups are context.
baseline: Median of the store's own peer gap over the previous 13 weeks (DQ-failed weeks excluded)
selection_reason: First family in interpretability order (peer_gap_threshold) with a candidate inside the 2% non-episode budget; smallest compliant threshold, then shortest persistence.
message: Store transactions are unusually low against the rest of the estate. Cause not established from available internal data.
data_required: Footfall, store operating logs, local events and competitor activity (Phase 8 DR01-DR11)
adaptation: Phase 8 named 'matched peer stores' without defining them; the peer group is every other store (leave-one-out), excluding DQ-failed stores. Two rules raise WARNING, each selected on the same noise budget: the peer-gap threshold with persistence, and the Phase 8 change-point test (weekly series, switched off once the store is back within half the step). CRITICAL needs both to agree in the same week, or the persistence, breadth or exposure criteria.

grain: estate, region, store format x retail week
grain_reason: Management-level view of broad softness; regions and formats show whether a store alert is local or part of a wider move.
baseline: Median of the entity's own YoY over the previous 13 weeks
selection_reason: First family in interpretability order (yoy_vs_trend_threshold) with a candidate inside the 2% non-episode budget; smallest compliant threshold, then shortest persistence.
message: Transactions are below their recent year-on-year trend. Cause not established from available internal data.
data_required: Market and footfall data; region-level store reports
adaptation: Same concept (YoY against its recent range) with a robust statistic (median and MAD). Region and format grains added, as the Phase 9 brief requires.

name: Availability deterioration
phase8_metric: Availability by category and by supplier
phase8_baseline: Same weeks last year and the previous 8 weeks
phase8_threshold: Below both baselines for 4 consecutive weeks (concept); to be calibrated
implemented_metric: Availability (in-stock cells / ranged cells) minus both the same week last year and the trailing 8-week mean, in percentage points (the smaller gap)
grain: category and supplier x retail week
grain_reason: Availability is a stock-system ratio over thousands of store-SKU cells; category and supplier are where buying and replenishment act.
baseline: Same retail week last year AND trailing 8 weeks (both must be breached)
selection_reason: First family in interpretability order (availability_gap_pp) with a candidate inside the 2% non-episode budget; smallest compliant threshold, then shortest persistence.
message: Availability is below both last year and its recent level. Supplier or ordering responsibility is not established.
data_required: Purchase orders, ASNs, DC stock, ordering parameters (Phase 8 DR12-DR21)
adaptation: Below BOTH baselines, as in Phase 8. The back-test selected 2 consecutive weeks instead of the concept's 4 (4 weeks is in the sensitivity table).

name: Top-seller full-week stock-outs
phase8_metric: Full-week stock-outs and weeks of cover on the top 10% of SKUs by sales
phase8_baseline: Prior-year level for the same SKUs
phase8_threshold: Any top-seller SKU with a full-week stock-out in 2 consecutive weeks (concept)
implemented_metric: Number of stores where the SKU had a full-week stock-out (no stock all week, nothing received)
grain_reason: Lost sales concentrate in a few high sellers (Phase 6); watching every SKU would drown them in noise. Top sellers are re-ranked every week from the trailing 13 weeks, so new launches enter.
baseline: Prior-year level is zero for almost every SKU, so the rule is an absolute count with persistence
selection_reason: First family in interpretability order (stores_out_count) with a candidate inside the 2% non-episode budget; smallest compliant threshold, then shortest persistence.
evidence_level: Observed change (monitoring alert); the no-stock-no-sales mechanism is root-cause evidence (Phase 6 D03)
message: A top-selling SKU has had no stock all week in several stores. Why stock ran out is not established.
data_required: Daily stock positions, purchase orders and ASNs for the SKU (Phase 8 DR12, DR15, DR16)
adaptation: Full-week stock-outs of the top 10% of SKUs, as in Phase 8. Weeks of cover not implemented: it needs daily demand and open orders (Phase 8 data requirement). The baseline is zero stock-outs, the same test as the Phase 8 threshold concept.

name: Faulty-return deterioration
phase8_metric: 'Faulty' returned units per 100 sold, by store, supplier and sale month
phase8_threshold: Rate increase unlikely under the prior-year rate (a conditional binomial test as in Phase 6); significance level and minimum volume to be set
implemented_metric: 'Faulty' returned units per 100 units sold (return-date basis, so no future returns are used), trailing 4 weeks
grain: Electronics & Tech at estate and store level, trailing 4 weeks, evaluated weekly
grain_reason: 'Faulty' returns are a few units per store-week; a single week cannot be tested. A 4-week window against the same 4 weeks last year gives counts a binomial test can judge.
baseline: Same 4 retail weeks last year; conditional binomial test of this year's share of the two years' Faulty units
selection_reason: First family in interpretability order (binomial_excess) with a candidate inside the 2% non-episode budget; smallest compliant threshold, then shortest persistence.
message: Faulty-return activity exceeds expected range and requires investigation.
data_required: QA inspection, batch or serial numbers, supplier RMA and warranty data (Phase 8 DR22-DR28)
adaptation: Phase 8 proposed store-month; Phase 9 requires the retail week, so a trailing 4-week window is tested weekly against the same 4 weeks last year (return-date basis). Supplier and product splits are context (ew05_return_context.csv), not separate alerts. An estate category level is added.

name: Gross-margin deterioration
phase8_threshold: A step down that persists for 4 weeks (concept); to be calibrated
implemented_metric: Gross margin % (trailing 4 weeks) minus the same 4 weeks last year, in percentage points; gross margin EUR change shown alongside
grain: category x retail week, trailing 4 weeks
grain_reason: Margin swings with promotion pulses week to week; a 4-week window smooths the pulse without hiding a sustained step.
selection_reason: First family in interpretability order (margin_gap_pp) with a candidate inside the 2% non-episode budget; smallest compliant threshold, then shortest persistence.
message: Gross margin % is below last year for the same weeks. The driver (price, mix, promotions, cost) is not established.
data_required: Promotion plan and supplier funding, cost price changes (Phase 8 DR29-DR31)
adaptation: Gross margin % of 4-week windows against the same weeks last year; GM EUR change reported beside it and tracked separately from revenue.

name: Unusual promotion behaviour
phase8_metric: Discount rate, promotion share and promotion events by category
phase8_baseline: The approved promotion plan (once DR29 exists); prior year until then
phase8_threshold: Actual above plan by an agreed tolerance (to be set by Commercial)
implemented_metric: Discount rate (discount / gross sales, trailing 4 weeks) minus the same 4 weeks last year, in percentage points; promotion share and promoted lines shown alongside
grain: category x retail week, trailing 4 weeks
grain_reason: Promotions run in pulses of about 3 weeks; a same-week comparison with last year compares pulse weeks with non-pulse weeks. A trailing 4-week window compares like with like.
baseline: Same 4 retail weeks last year (no approved promotion plan exists in the data; Phase 8 DR29)
selection_reason: First family in interpretability order (discount_gap_pp) with a candidate inside the 2% non-episode budget; smallest compliant threshold, then shortest persistence.
message: Promotion depth is well above last year for the same weeks. Its effect on sales and margin is not established.
data_required: Promotion calendar with objectives and planned depth (Phase 8 DR29, DR30)
adaptation: The approved promotion plan (DR29) does not exist, so the prior year is the baseline, as Phase 8 allows until then. Discount rate is the alert metric; promotion share and promotion lines are context.

name: Data completeness and quality
phase8_metric: Receipts per store-day and returns per store-day against expected ranges; missing snapshots
phase8_baseline: Same weekday over the previous 8 weeks
phase8_threshold: Zero or near-zero counts on a trading day (concept)
grain: store x retail week (plus estate roll-up)
grain_reason: Data arrives per store and day; a store-week gate can hold exactly the alerts whose data is damaged.
baseline: Fixed tolerances; row counts against the store's trailing 13-week median
selection_reason: First family in interpretability order (dq_gate_fail) with a candidate inside the 2% non-episode budget; smallest compliant threshold, then shortest persistence.
message: Data for this store-week failed the DQ gate; business alerts are held until the data is complete.
data_required: Load logs and extract batch schedule
adaptation: Phase 8 proposed a daily store-day check; the weekly run applies a store-week gate whose first check (C1) counts trading days with no sales, so a day-level gap is caught. A daily run would reuse C1 per day.
